set.reason: Gemini confines its necessity argument to sexagesimal-format items. The actual criterion does not prescribe that format: decimal or whole-degree measures support angle addition and bisector calculations without minute/second conversion.

set.reason: Gemini uses quadrant/axis features to assign coordinates in one diagram method. Coordinate differences and area can instead be computed from already supplied points without quadrant classification, so these features prepare rather than universally precede the task.
set.scope: segment lengths and areas from coordinates

set.reason: The criterion explicitly permits triangles OR rectangles. Both external reviews turn that alternative into an unconditional requirement, but an L-shaped orthogonal figure can be split entirely into rectangles. Preserve triangle area as a component of the triangular-piece route without making every composite-area task use it.
set.scope: Calculating triangular pieces in a triangular partition of a composite area

set.reason: Segment sums, comparison and midpoint relations form useful analogies for angle sums, comparison and bisection. Angle operations can be introduced directly from rays and measures.
set.scope: analogy between segment and angle operations

set.reason: Gemini confines its necessity argument to sexagesimal-format items. The actual criterion does not prescribe that format: decimal or whole-degree measures support angle addition and bisector calculations without minute/second conversion.
set.scope: Degree-minute-second measures as one format for angle arithmetic

set.reason: Gemini uses quadrant/axis features to assign coordinates in one diagram method. Coordinate differences and area can instead be computed from already supplied points without quadrant classification, so these features prepare rather than universally precede the task.
set.scope: segment lengths and areas from coordinates

set.reason: The criterion explicitly permits triangles OR rectangles. Both external reviews turn that alternative into an unconditional requirement, but an L-shaped orthogonal figure can be split entirely into rectangles. Preserve triangle area as a component of the triangular-piece route without making every composite-area task use it.
set.scope: Calculating triangular pieces in a triangular partition of a composite area

set.reason: The broad description allows partition into studied shapes, so a trapezoid partition is a useful optional method. The explicit triangle/rectangle criterion and rectangle-only examples show it is not universally required.
set.scope: Calculating trapezoid pieces when a composite figure is partitioned into familiar trapezoids
